item.title: Why do I hate Dialectics so much?
item.description:
1. Superficiality, Hindering Deep Analysis:

    • Problem: Simply stating that “everything has two sides” is like applying a label, stopping further thought and exploration. Without digging deeper into what those two sides are, the specific conditions that generate them, and which side is more important in a specific context, how to weigh them.
    • Analysis: This assertion simplifies a complex issue into a simple formula, masking the deeper causes, mechanisms, and influences behind the problem. It easily satisfies people with a superficial understanding, lacking the drive to trace the root cause, ultimately leading to a shallow grasp of the issue and preventing the proposal of effective solutions. For example, when discussing the impact of a policy, if one only says “it has pros and cons,” without analyzing what the specific benefits are, what the drawbacks are, and what impact they have on which groups, the actual effectiveness of the policy cannot be assessed.

  2. Relativism Run Amok, Blurring Objective Standards:
item.content:encoded:
1. Superficiality, Hindering Deep Analysis:

    • Problem: Simply stating that “everything has two sides” is like applying a label, stopping further thought and exploration. Without digging deeper into what those two sides are, the specific conditions that generate them, and which side is more important in a specific context, how to weigh them.
    • Analysis: This assertion simplifies a complex issue into a simple formula, masking the deeper causes, mechanisms, and influences behind the problem. It easily satisfies people with a superficial understanding, lacking the drive to trace the root cause, ultimately leading to a shallow grasp of the issue and preventing the proposal of effective solutions. For example, when discussing the impact of a policy, if one only says “it has pros and cons,” without analyzing what the specific benefits are, what the drawbacks are, and what impact they have on which groups, the actual effectiveness of the policy cannot be assessed.

  2. Relativism Run Amok, Blurring Objective Standards:

    • Problem: Overemphasizing “duality” easily slides into relativism—the idea that “nothing is absolute”—believing that every viewpoint has its own rationality, thereby blurring objective criteria for judgment and the lines between right and wrong.
    • Analysis: While acknowledging that the world is complex does not mean abandoning judgment of right and wrong, it does not mean that “duality” equals “two sides are equally valid.” In fields like ethics and scientific truth, objective standards exist. Overemphasizing relativity weakens our ability to distinguish truth from falsehood, good from evil, and can even provide seemingly rational explanations for immoral behavior. For instance, just because a certain cultural custom has its “reason for existence,” one cannot assume that every custom is equal, while ignoring whether it infringes upon human rights.

  3. Defending Errors, Escaping Responsibility:

    • Problem: Utilizing the “dialectical view” to find excuses for obvious errors, suggesting that as long as one can find a little “positive” aspect, it can offset the negative impact, thereby escaping responsibility and condemnation.
    • Analysis: This assertion confuses merit and fault, blurring boundaries that should be clearly distinguished. Even if a person or action contributes in certain aspects, this cannot be used to deny or mitigate the harm caused by their error. For example, the statement, “Although he embezzled, he also contributed to the local area,” is an attempt to use a localized, unrelated “contribution” to mask the essence of his corruption and the damage it caused to society.

  4. Hindering Action, Leading to Indecision:

    • Problem: Always thinking that “everything has two sides” might cause people to focus too much on potential negative consequences, amplifying risks, and thus making it difficult to make a decision, leading to missed opportunities.
    • Analysis: Rational decision-making requires weighing pros and cons, but excessive emphasis on “duality” can lead to mental rigidity, trapping one in a dilemma of “half good, half bad,” making it impossible to focus on the main contradiction and the goal. For example, if an entrepreneur is always thinking about various possibilities of failure in starting a business, while ignoring potential opportunities, they may never take the first step.

  5. Being Used for Thought Control:

    • Problem: Power holders utilize the “dialectical view” to demand that individuals simultaneously accept contradictory viewpoints, such as “must… and must…” (both… and…), which appears comprehensive on the surface, but is actually designed to maintain their rule, suppress dissent, and strip away the ability to think independently.
    • Analysis: In this scenario, the “dialectical view” becomes a tool used to create cognitive dissonance, forcing people to submit to the authority’s logic, even if that logic is chaotic and contradictory. It strips the individual of the ability to judge right from wrong, making it difficult for them to question unreasonable phenomena. For example, certain propaganda slogans might simultaneously emphasize “hard work and struggle” and “life happiness,” yet fail to provide a concrete path to achieving this balance, leaving people feeling confused and powerless.

  6. Creating a False Sense of Equality, Masking Power Asymmetry:

    • Problem: When there is a clear gap in power and social inequality, using “everything has two sides” to blur the actual status and situation of both parties, thereby masking the interests of the dominant side and ignoring the plight of the weaker side.
    • Analysis: This assertion appears objectively neutral, but it ignores structural inequality. For example, in a labor-management dispute, saying “the boss and the employee both have their difficulties” seems balanced, but it ignores that the boss controls the means of production and decision-making power, while the employee’s bargaining power is relatively weaker. This discussion of “duality” is actually defending the powerful, maintaining the unfair status quo.

  7. Weakening the Necessity of Value Judgment:

    • Problem: Overemphasizing “duality” easily makes people feel that everything is “more or less the same,” without clear distinctions between superior and inferior, thereby weakening the willingness and ability to make clear value judgments.
    • Analysis: This leads to the blurring of boundaries regarding good and bad, superior and inferior, good and evil, increasing tolerance for errors and injustices. For example, when facing a controversial technology, if one only emphasizes that it “has both convenience and risk,” without deeply assessing whether the risk far outweighs the benefit, it may lead to blind promotion, bringing potential harm.

  8. Degenerating into Rhetoric, Not a Tool for Thought:

    • Problem: The “dialectical view” and “everything has two sides” are sometimes simplified into a catchphrase, merely to appear “objective” and “profound,” while lacking genuine thought and analysis.
    • Analysis: In this case, “dialectics” becomes a label, a universal phrase that can be used to handle various situations, but it lacks deep logic and argumentation behind it. People may habitually throw out these concepts without seriously considering the essence of the problem and the solution, hindering the development of critical thinking.

  9. Being Abused Under Information Asymmetry:

    • Problem: The party that holds the information advantage may deliberately present only the side favorable to itself, and then use “everything has two sides” to imply that there is “another side,” but in reality, that other side may be intentionally hidden or distorted, thereby misleading the public.
    • Analysis: In this scenario, “duality” becomes a tool for manipulating public opinion. For example, some merchants might promote the advantages of a product, and then use “any product has its limitations” to mask its serious defects, leveraging information asymmetry to mislead consumers.

  10. Cultural Inertia and Conservatism:

    • Problem: Overemphasizing the “dialectical view” is sometimes used to oppose any form of change and innovation, because any new thing inevitably carries uncertainty and potential risk.
    • Analysis: This way of thinking easily falls into conservatism, fearing the “other side” that change might bring, even if not changing might bring greater harm. For example, when facing a reform measure aimed at solving social injustice, some people might use “any reform has pros and cons” to obstruct its implementation, while ignoring that not reforming could lead to further intensification of social contradictions.

item.title: Some thoughts on Christmas 2024
item.description: This text describes the desolate scenes in some Chinese cities during Christmas, as well as the extreme nationalist incident of burning Christmas trees that occurred in Chengdu and Chongqing. The author distinguishes himself from these people by giving them nicknames and discusses the social phenomena behind this behavior.
item.content:encoded:
It is a desolate Christmas. Some businesses have secretly put up a little decoration, but more often, there is simply no Christmas atmosphere.

The first-tier cities like Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen are doing quite well. It seems the businesses have received a notice and have started decorating for Christmas again.

However, in Chengdu and Chongqing, there are extreme nationalists burning Christmas trees. This is both a coincidence and an inevitability.

I searched for related videos and saw that the bullet comments and reviews are praising and cheering for this behavior. Of course, I know this might be the algorithm doing evil, but it cannot be denied that a large number of people think this way.

To allow myself to live at a higher dimension, I have given them a new nickname: ⏰

The benefit of giving them a nickname is that it allows you to distinguish yourself from them, and not feel any empathy for them. From now on, you don’t want to pity them, nor do you want to communicate with them. This further practices my NPC theory. NPC Philosophy

item.title: Don't give the sacred artifact to pigs and dogs, lest it trample it and turn around to bite you.
item.description:
Deeply ingrained beliefs formed over many years cannot be awakened by mere words or phrases.

Abandoning Medicine for Literature Cannot Save the Chinese People

The two most difficult things in this world are: first, putting other people’s money into your own pocket; and second, putting your own thoughts into other people’s heads. The first thing touches people’s interests, and the second thing touches their soul.

item.content:encoded:

  • Next, we need to purchase a domain name and create a blog for the product itself.

  • Fixed the issue where tags weren’t refreshing.
  • Added the last modified time.
  • We can consider setting the proportion of fetch to be a little smaller.

  • Currently, it supports images.
  • Using left/right swipe gestures for file management.
  • We don’t know how to manage the article covers because each theme is different.

Perfecting details, taking screenshots, preparing the landing page.

1116

Everything has a cost, but some people see the cost and are willing to pay it. Some people don’t see the cost, or they think there will be no cost at all. And when the time comes for them to pay the price, they will only complain about the unfairness of heaven (or: fate).

item.title: What does it mean to have incompatible core values?
item.description:
You revere natural law, he worships authority, This is a difference in worldview;

You stand on the side of conscience, he stands on the side of the strong, This is a difference in values;

Your effort is for an ideal life, His effort is to be superior to others, This is a difference in philosophy of life.

item.title: Tolerate the fool, understand the fool, harvest the fool.
item.description: This article explores the complex relationship between influencing higher-level interests and changing lower-tier perceptions, pointing out that the two are actually intrinsically linked, because lower-level perceptions form the foundation of higher-level interests.
item.content:encoded: Do not disturb the interests of the upper stratum, nor should you disturb the mindset of the lower stratum. Disturbing the interests of the upper stratum is akin to taking his life, while disturbing the beliefs of the lower stratum is like digging up his ancestral grave, and the beliefs of the lower stratum are precisely the source of the upper stratum’s interests.

item.title: A little insight from Waterdrop
item.description:
Suidi Chou is listed in the US.

Prospectus

Prospectus link: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1823986/000119312521154899/d95574d424b4.htm#rom95574_23

Core Content

  1. Profitability Status: This company, which occupies the highest moral ground, earned 14.4 billion RMB in 2020 alone, averaging 7,300 RMB per patient.
  2. Donation Status: As of December 31, 2020, over 340 million people have donated to more than 1.7 million patients through Suidi Medical Crowdfunding, accumulating over 37 billion RMB. The average donation per person is 100 RMB, and the average amount received per patient is 21,000 RMB. However, the actual amount received by patients may be less because the company needs to generate profit.
  3. Tencent’s Stake: Tencent currently holds a beneficial ownership stake of 22.1% in Suidi Chou.
  4. Tencent’s Revenue: In 2020, Tencent earned a total of 210 million RMB from Suidi Chou through payment processing fees, advertising, and marketing fees.

Personal Reflection

Every company aims for profit, no matter how noble its banner may be. The world itself is extremely cruel.

item.title: Don't Just Focus on Your Weaknesses: The Theory of Comparative Advantage
item.description: Big goals are easier to achieve than small ones because problems cannot completely block your view of the big picture. Successful people always know how to put themselves in a “necessary” situation; without achieving their goals, they will never be happy. When you set limits for yourself, you will try to reach those limits. You should not only take responsibility for your failures but also for your successes. If you believe that success is unrepeatable, you lose the opportunity to improve your self-worth. A person who gives 110% effort and actively eliminates all excuses is bound to succeed. You need a good coach, someone who can maximize your potential using their own experience. The first person to focus on their weaknesses will not gain wealth. Whether it’s passive defense or active offense in a competition makes a world of difference. Many people have lost the joy of life and the opportunity to become wealthy by trying too hard to eliminate their weaknesses. The price you must pay to acquire wealth is time. But this is not comparable to the time you earn through wealth. Wealth allows you to think calmly about the meaning of life without financial concerns. +++

item.title: No miracle happens without adventure.
item.description: • We often forget that continuing along the path we have already taken also carries risks. This path gives us a sense of familiarity, but it doesn’t guarantee safety either. • Life is a competition. Those who don’t take risks cannot achieve success. • On this planet, there is no “guaranteed win,” only “opportunity.” • Take action immediately! Because you can never be perfectly prepared for success. • The only person in the world who never makes a mistake is the person who never does anything. (Theodore Roosevelt) • The pain brought by uncertainty is much stronger than the pain of certainty. • Every course of action carries risks and requires a cost. But compared to the comfort of doing nothing, the long-term risks and costs are much smaller. (John Fitzgerald Kennedy) • If you are afraid of losing, you will never gain. • Go take risks; you can’t fall from the ground.

item.title: Many difficulties are excuses; in reality, we do not believe that we can succeed.
item.description:
Energy tips build self-confidence by keeping a success diary every day.

  • Our self-confidence determines whether we dare to take risks.
  • Without taking risks, growth is impossible.
  • Overall, our thoughts, the education we receive, and the environment around us are not conducive to cultivating our self-confidence. A healthy self-assessment means confidence. Keeping a success diary makes you aware of how excellent you are.
  • When writing a diary, you learn to focus on your strengths.
  • After some time, you will start to discover your strengths and think: I can write this into my success diary.
  • Our expectations determine what we will achieve. Our self-confidence again determines our expectations.

item.title: The person who gives you responsibility also gives you power.
item.description:
Most people tend to deflect responsibility. When people don’t want to take responsibility, we always hear them use these 3 reasons to evade the blame:

  1. “It’s the genes’ fault.”
  2. “It’s the parents’ fault.”
  3. “It’s the objective environment’s fault.”

item.title: Who can teach us how to become wealthy? Is it our parents?
item.description:
Our values and goals must be consistent. Optimism allows you to see the positive side of things, while confidence gives you the faith to overcome the dark side of things.

Confidence refers to a person knowing, based on their own experiences, that they can rely on themselves when facing challenges.

To own a money-making machine, rather than being a money-making machine your entire life.
